[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Alexander was born before 1747 to [[Glasgow-1239|Andrew Glasgow]] and [[Clerk-314|Isobel Clerk]] in Kirknewton, Linlithgowshire, Scotland <ref>https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-P5V</ref>

He married [[Cunningham-20926|Agnes Cunninghame (abt.1755-)]] and had his son [[Glasgow-1481|Andrew Glasgow (bef.1776-)]] in Saint Cuthberts, Edinburgh, Midlothian, Scotland<ref>https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC4-727</ref>
== Research Notes ==
=== Parish household review, 23 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-1482|Agnes Glasgow]] → [[Glasgow-1321|Alexander Glasgow]]: 87% → 97% (confident). Agnes’s 1774 St Cuthbert’s entry identifies Alexander Glasgow, brewer’s servant, and Agness Cunninghame at Cross Causeway, with birth 15 July and baptism 30 July. Andrew’s newly interpreted 1775/1776 entry independently records the same couple and trade at Grange. The consecutive children, parental combination, occupation and compatible Edinburgh residences identify the adult household represented by Alexander-1321. 97% concerns Agnes’s father as the adult Alexander/Agnes Cunningham householder. Identifying him with the 1747 Kirknewton child is a separate upstream inference, now assessed at 76%. It does not establish Agnes’s later Smart identity or an 1810 burial. Indexes of the same event are not independent witnesses; the 1774 and 1776 births are separate events. Original register images uninspected.

[[Glasgow-1481|Andrew Glasgow]] → [[Glasgow-1321|Alexander Glasgow]]: 64% → 97% (confident). St Cuthbert’s OPR 685_2/9 item 1 p.275 records Andrew born 30 December 1775, baptised 5 January 1776, parents Alexander Glasgow and Agnes Cunningham, father a brewer’s servant, residence Grange. These literal fields resolve the previous missing-parent limitation. The same parental couple and trade in Agnes’s separate 1774 Cross Causeway entry identify one adult household represented by Alexander-1321. 97% concerns Andrew’s father in the Edinburgh adult household. It does not prove Alexander’s 1747 Kirknewton childhood, Andrew’s later 1790 merchant identity, or other attached children. Andrew cannot be the 1779 adult signatory because he was three. The companion index’s birth year 1776 is baptism-derived; retain the reviewed 1775 birth date. Original register images uninspected.

[[Glasgow-1321|Alexander Glasgow]] → [[Glasgow-1336|Andrew Glasgow]]: 95% → 76% (probable). Alexander-1321 represents the documented 1774–1776 Edinburgh brewer’s-servant household with Agnes Cunningham. The 1747 Kirknewton baptism names Andrew Glasgow and Isobel Clerk; 95% remains the conditional assessment of that child’s parent clause. Age about 27 in 1774 and compatible regional chronology support identifying the child with the adult, but no held record connects the childhood to the later occupation or spouse. The full adult-to-Andrew-1336 placement is therefore 76%. The graph percentage assesses the complete adult-profile father proposition. The prior 95% concerned only the record-defined 1747 child and is preserved with that scope, not disproved. The 1751 Glasgow Alexander entry remains an unresolved comparison, not a demonstrated rival. No father is replaced and no vital field or mother is changed. Original register images uninspected.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1336]] is assessed at 95% (proved). Alexander’s 1747 Kirknewton child account names Andrew Glasgow and Isobel Clerk. The selected Andrew is attached to that same named spouse and family, so the full couple identifies the record father substantially better than the older biography’s inconsistent Andrew profile link.

Record-defined 1747 child and Clerk household; Andrew’s 1714 childhood and the stale Glasgow-1239 link are not proved by this assessment.
